artifacts.summary: Five-phase re-scoped plan: promote the machine-checked L-plus incompleteness refutation to a compiled library module, pin it in the C2 axiom baseline and docs/theorem-index.md, correct the two READMEs that present (C1') as an unqualified repair, and spawn the substrate redesign plus the L-plus carrier normalization as dependent tasks. No compression proof is attempted.

memory_candidates.content: Design rule for branching/state-sharing certificate condition sets in modal-temporal decidability devices: a local-coherence clause that quantifies its witness over the sharing equivalence class at the LABEL'S OWN time forces every member of that class to agree on the labelled formula (read the clause twice -- once at i with k := j, once at j with k := j by reflexivity -- and the two biconditionals share a right-hand side). That silently makes the corresponding truth-value a function of the world state, which makes the device INCOMPLETE for any validity the state does not determine. Quantifying over the class at t+1 or t-1 instead does not have this consequence, which is why an `until` clause can be defect-free while a `since` clause is not. Diagnostic: for each condition, ask which time's class it quantifies over relative to the label it constrains. Repair is at the substrate level (an explicit transition relation on indices, separate from the sharing relation), never a re-wording of the condition. Corollary for planning: a condition set with no landed example satisfying ALL conditions simultaneously at non-trivial sharing is unvalidated -- per-condition non-vacuity witnesses do not catch this class of defect, and a compression/completeness proof planned against such a set can be planned against a false statement.
